**Refined prompt:** Diagnose why the React client throws `Cannot read property 'slug' of undefined` immediately after `POST /articles` while the server logs nothing — answering as a maintainer of this NestJS RealWorld API, citing the responsible lines, and naming the fix rather than speculating.

## What's wrong

`POST /api/articles` is the one handler in the codebase that returns a **bare entity instead of the `{ article }` envelope**.

`src/article/article.service.ts:170` — `create()` is typed `Promise<ArticleEntity>`, and `:186` returns `newArticle` directly. Every sibling method wraps: `findOne` returns `{article}` (`:98`), `update` (`:194`), `favorite` (`:144`), `addComment` (`:111`).

`src/article/article.controller.ts:52-54` — `create()` passes it straight through and, unlike `findOne` (`:39`) or `findAll` (`:25`), carries **no return-type annotation**. That missing `: Promise<ArticleRO>` is why the compiler never caught the mismatch.

So the wire response is:

```json
{ "id": 7, "slug": "how-to-train-your-dragon-x8f2k1", "title": "...", ... }
```

The frontend reads `response.article.slug` → `response.article` is `undefined` → the TypeError. **The server logs nothing because nothing failed server-side**: the row was written, the status was 201. The bug is entirely in the response shape.

This is LESSONS.md's recorded incident #57 — the rule there is that a handler whose return type isn't a `*RO` interface is a bug even when it works in Postman.

## Fix

```ts
// article.service.ts:170,186
async create(userId: number, articleData: CreateArticleDto): Promise<ArticleRO> {
  ...
  return {article: newArticle};
}

// article.controller.ts:52 — annotate so it can't regress
async create(@User('id') userId: number, @Body('article') articleData: CreateArticleDto): Promise<ArticleRO> {
```

## Two things that will bite the moment you fix this

I read `create()` closely and there are adjacent defects in the same six lines:

1. **`body` is never written.** `create()` assigns `title`, `description`, `slug`, `tagList`, `comments` (`article.service.ts:173-177`) and skips `articleData.body`. `ArticleEntity.body` is `@Column({default: ''})` (`article.entity.ts:20-21`), so the article saves with an empty body, silently.
2. **`author` is absent from the created response.** `newArticle` is saved at `:179`, *before* the author is attached at `:181-184` via the inverse side — so the returned object has no `author`. The client's next render of `article.author.username` crashes the same way. Note the re-fetch won't save you: `findOne()` (`:97`) passes no `relations: ['author']`, and `author` is a non-eager `@ManyToOne` (`article.entity.ts:37-38`), so it's `undefined` there too.

Want me to apply the envelope fix alone, or all three?
